gp2-vs-gp3-ebs-cost-and-how-to-migrate.h.text:
EBS Volume Cost Advisor · guide

gp2 vs gp3: EBS volume cost and how to migrate

Short answer: for almost every general-purpose volume, gp3 is 20% cheaper than gp2 and faster by default, and you can switch live. The savings that matter most are elsewhere: provisioned-IOPS volumes billing for IOPS they never use, and volumes nobody has attached for months.

What each type costs (us-east-1 list prices, illustrative)

  • gp2: $0.10 per GB-month. Performance is tied to size: 3 IOPS per GB (100 minimum, 16,000 maximum), bursting to 3,000 IOPS below 1,000 GB until burst credits run out.
  • gp3: $0.08 per GB-month with 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s included; $0.005 per extra IOPS-month (up to 16,000) and $0.04 per extra MiB/s-month (up to 1,000).
  • io1 / io2: $0.125 per GB-month plus $0.065 per provisioned IOPS-month. io2 is the same price as io1 with higher durability.
  • st1 / sc1: $0.045 / $0.015 per GB-month, throughput-optimised HDD, capped at 500 / 250 IOPS.

Where the money is

  • gp2 to gp3: $0.02 per GB-month on every volume. A fleet of 50 TB of gp2 is about $1,000 a month.
  • io1 to gp3: a 1,000 GB io1 at 20,000 IOPS costs $1,425 a month; if the observed peak is 6,000 IOPS, gp3 at 7,200 IOPS costs about $103.
  • Over-provisioned gp3: volumes set to 6,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s that peak at 800 IOPS pay $20 a month each for nothing.
  • Unattached volumes: a volume in the available state bills the full price for no work.

Measure and migrate

  1. List volumes: aws ec2 describe-volumes --query 'Volumes[].[VolumeId,VolumeType,Size,Iops,Throughput,State]' --output text.
  2. For each, take the busiest week's peak of VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps divided by the period in seconds (use a 1 or 5 minute period), and of VolumeReadBytes + VolumeWriteBytes in MiB/s.
  3. Paste rows into the advisor, or run node cli.mjs analyze volumes.csv. It prints a modify-volume command per volume.
  4. Change one non-critical volume first; the type change is live but the volume spends time in the optimizing state.

Questions

Is gp3 cheaper than gp2?

Yes for nearly every volume: gp3 costs $0.08 per GB-month against $0.10 for gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s, which gp2 only reaches at 1,000 GB. Extra gp3 IOPS cost $0.005 per IOPS-month and extra throughput $0.04 per MiB/s-month.

Can I switch gp2 to gp3 without downtime?

Yes. Elastic Volumes changes type, IOPS and throughput on an attached volume. Run aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id vol-xxxx --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 125; the volume is usable while it optimizes, and you can modify a volume roughly once every six hours.

Why is my io1 volume so expensive?

io1 and io2 charge $0.065 per provisioned IOPS-month on top of $0.125 per GB. A volume provisioned at 20,000 IOPS but peaking at 6,000 pays for 14,000 IOPS it never uses. If the peak fits gp3's 16,000 IOPS and 1,000 MiB/s ceiling, gp3 costs a small fraction of that.

EBS VOLUME COST ADVISOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Are your EBS volumes the wrong type?

Paste one row per volume — type, size, provisioned IOPS, observed peak IOPS and throughput — and get the cheapest type that still covers the peak (gp2 → gp3, io1 → gp3), the ready-to-paste aws ec2 modify-volume command, gp2 volumes that depend on burst credits and unattached volumes still billing you.

Nothing is uploaded and AWS is never contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. The peak is the number you supply, so a spike shorter than your sampling period is invisible.

Prefer a CLI, or want a CI check?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs analyze volumes.csv
cat volumes.csv | node cli.mjs analyze -
node cli.mjs analyze volumes.csv --fail-on warn      # exit 1 on any waste or throttling
node cli.mjs analyze volumes.csv --headroom 1.5 --json --prices my-prices.json

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: gp2 vs gp3: EBS cost and how to migrate.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Prices are illustrative and dated; edit them with --prices in the CLI. Snapshots, other regions, Savings Plans, multi-attach and Block Express limits above 64,000 IOPS are not modelled.

Common questions

Does this connect to my AWS account?

No. It reads the rows you paste and never contacts AWS. It cannot see your real invoice, snapshots, Savings Plans or free tier, so every dollar figure is the rows you pasted times list prices you can edit.

How do I get the numbers?

Size, type, provisioned IOPS and throughput come from aws ec2 describe-volumes. Peak IOPS is the maximum over a busy week of (VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps) divided by the period in seconds in CloudWatch, and peak MiB/s is (VolumeReadBytes + VolumeWriteBytes) divided by the period, in MiB. Use a one-minute or five-minute period, not an hourly average that hides the peak.

Is gp3 always cheaper than gp2?

Almost always for the same size: gp3 is 20% cheaper per GB and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s. A large gp2 volume that gets more than 3,000 IOPS from its size (3 IOPS per GB above 1,000 GB) can need extra gp3 IOPS to match, at $0.005 per IOPS-month, so the tool sizes gp3 from your observed peak instead of assuming.

Does changing the volume type cause downtime?

No. Elastic Volumes changes the type, size, IOPS and throughput of a volume while it stays attached and in use. It enters an optimizing state for a while, you can change a volume about once every six hours, and you should still try one non-critical volume first.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page analyses the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.
